title: Counting fish you can't all see
hook: How do you count a lake's fish without catching every one?

doesNotKnow: how to count animals nobody can see all of
that the marked share of a catch estimates the marked share of the whole lake

misconception: The number you catch is roughly the population.
objective: The learner can explain that if 100 marked fish are mixed into a lake and 5 of a 50-fish net are marked, the lake holds about 100 x 50 / 5 = 1,000 fish, and that single nets wobble around that estimate.

claims.text: If marked fish are mixed evenly into a lake, the marked share of a netted sample is about the marked share of the lake, so the lake holds about (marked x caught) / (marked in the catch) fish (Lincoln-Petersen estimate).
claims.source: Seber, The Estimation of Animal Abundance, 1982 (Lincoln-Petersen). Ratio argument: R / C ~ M / N.

claims.text: 100 marked, 50 caught, 5 marked in the catch gives 100 x 50 / 5 = 1,000 fish.
claims.source: Arithmetic; Demo.tsx computes it from M, C and MARKED[0].

claims.text: Model (stated on the stage): a toy lake of 1,000 fish, 100 already marked and mixed in; each net takes 50 fish. The method assumes a closed population, even mixing and marks that are not lost.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; brief life #42. Closed population, random mixing, no mark loss (Seber 1982).

claims.text: In the five seeded nets, 5, 4, 7, 9 and 3 of 50 fish are marked, giving estimates of 1,000, 1,250, 714, 556 and 1,667; single estimates scatter around the true 1,000.
claims.source: Demo.tsx, mulberry32 seeds 11, 4, 15, 2, 20 (sample without replacement from 1,000 fish). Seed 11 was chosen so sample 1 matches the question's 5 marked; the other four were picked from a short list of seeds, not tuned for the spread. Values in artifacts/scratch/w5life/fish.mjs.

claims.text: Reveal: 'Nets wobble, so one estimate is a guess; several scatter around the true 1,000.'
claims.source: CONCERN from the fact-checker: the five stage estimates are 556 to 1,667 (mean 1,037); over 20,000 other nets of 50 only 53% fall within +/-25% of 1,000, and Lincoln-Petersen is biased upward at this size (mean of estimates 1,249). 'Cluster near' overstates; suggest 'scatter around' as the claim text c4 says. Added by fact-checker 2026-10-13; needs an independent check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Independent check of the pass-8 concern. The stage's five estimates are 1000, 1250, 714, 556, 1667 (0.56x to 1.67x the truth). My own node run (20,000 nets of 50 drawn without replacement, different seed): only 53.0% within +/-25% of 1,000, mean of estimates 1,252 (Lincoln-Petersen biased upward at R about 5), 74 nets caught no marked fish. 'Several cluster near the true 1,000' is not what the stage shows. Fix (builder): 'several scatter around the true 1,000' (as c4 says), or average them ('their average, 1,037, lands near 1,000'). | BUILDER 2026-10-13: stage and claim reworded per fact-check; needs re-verification. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Re-check: reveal now reads 'Nets wobble, so one estimate is a guess; several scatter around the true 1,000.' (Demo.tsx). The five stage estimates 556-1,667 (mean 1,037) do scatter around 1,000; 'scatter around' no longer overstates. Concern from pass 8/9 resolved.

recall.question: To estimate a lake's fish, 200 are marked and released. A later net of 40 fish has 8 marked. About how many fish are in the lake?
recall.why: 8 of 40 is 1 in 5 marked, so the 200 marked fish are about a fifth of the lake: 200 x 5 = 1,000.
